name: Holland M. Smith

roles.title: Commanding General, Fleet Marine Force, Pacific

summary: Wrote much of the American amphibious doctrine in the 1930s and then commanded the corps that executed it across the Central Pacific — Tarawa, the Marshalls, Saipan, Iwo Jima. Tarawa in November 1943 cost about a thousand Marines dead in seventy-six hours on an island of half a square mile, and the after-action reports from it changed naval gunfire, the length of the preparatory bombardment and the tracked landing vehicle. At Saipan in June 1944 he relieved an Army division commander, Major General Ralph Smith, in a row that reached the newspapers and left Army–Marine relations in the Pacific poisoned for the rest of the war.
